item.title: Toward a Spatial Dimension of Scenario Planning: Preparing Well for an Uncertain Future
item.description:
Alys Solly, Loris Servillo, Elisabetta Vitale Brovarone
Journal of Planning Literature
DOI: 10.1177/08854122261495991
The paper aims to shed light on how scenario planning can be usefully applied in spatial planning today at the various administrative levels. A mixed-method analytical approach is used to explore research articles, government reports, and policy documents dealing with spatialized scenario planning. The rationale behind the choice of the articles examined respects their spatial and policy-making foci. The study reveals that the institutional and governance framework of spatial planning, as well as the range of stakeholder participation, seem to influence the adoption and implementation of scenario planning procedures by planners and decision-makers in order to face future uncertainty.

item.title: Struggles of Inclusion in the Face of Power: A Review of Conflict in the Planning Literature
item.description:
Maged Senbel
Journal of Planning Literature
DOI: 10.1177/08854122261484595
Conflict is integral to planning yet understudied. This article undertakes a systematic review of the planning literature and traces conceptualizations of conflict over the decades. While conflict discourse has become more responsive to the increasing diversity of parties, it continues to variously leverage consensus, communicative, collaborative, therapeutic, and agonistic deliberative processes. Historical tensions persist surrounding the adequate inclusion of marginalized interests in the face of power disparities. A conflict typology is proposed, with distributive, integrative, differentiative and separative patterns. The typology can help planning scholars and practitioners situate their own work within an array of conflict engagement ontologies.
